Definition: from G1443; the Hebraistic (Hebrew) or Jewish (Chaldee) language:--Hebrew.
BiblicalUsage: Hebraïs is the Hebrew tongue itself, the language Paul speaks when he wants to be heard. In Acts 21:40 he stands on the stairs and speaks to the crowd in the Hebrew tongue, in Acts 22:2 the crowd keeps silence when they hear it, and in Acts 26:14 the voice from heaven speaks to him in the Hebrew tongue on the road to Damascus.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God speaks to a man in his own language at the turning point of his life, and the crowd goes quiet because the familiar tongue carries an unfamiliar message. I hold that the voice on the Damascus road chose Hebrew because Paul was a Hebrew, and grace always comes in the language the hearer knows best.
